subject: Next steps: Security exhibit onboarding, evidence onramp and inspection scope

Subject: Security exhibit kickoff and evidence cadence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Acme Health's procurement checklist we need to land on the security exhibit and a firm evidence cadence for SOC 2 and penetration testing. Two immediate asks: 1) a short summary of the inspection boundaries you can commit to (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and 2) the typical windows you offer for pen tests and what level of staging access is available.

We're trying to align procurement and infosec — timing is tight for our Q4 go-live. I attached a questionnaire that lists the fields we need filled. Can your team confirm by next Tuesday (2026-09-08)?

Also please loop legal if there are order form redlines we should expect. Happy to jump on a 30-min bridge if helpful.

Thanks,
Dana Moore
Senior Manager, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit kickoff and evidence cadence

Hi Dana — good to meet you over email. Thanks for the questionnaire; Monica (security & assurance) and Laura (legal) are looped.

Quick answers up front:
- Inspection boundaries: we support the full stack across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity (customer-isolated GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package). For SOC 2 and evidence purposes we can scope artifacts and sampling by tenancy and by deployment mode — e.g., if you will run on Dedicated we can provide tenant-scoped audit artifacts and ephemeral staging for pen tests.
- Pen test windows: standard cadence is a 48–72 hour notice for scheduled tests; we also support a 7-day notice for larger scopes. We offer ephemeral staging credentials scoped to the assessment and timeboxed with privilege elevation controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Monica will propose an evidence cadence matrix (what we can commit to weekly/monthly/quarterly).
2) Laura will call out any MSA/order form language that typically needs redline (SOC 2 attestation references, pen test definitions, inspection rights).
3) Can we schedule a 30-min call Wednesday 9/9 or Thursday 9/10 to finalize the first deliverables?

I've attached our order form redline draft so you can see the current positions.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Assurance Programs
Redwood Inference

> - Pen test windows: standard cadence is a 48–72 hour notice for scheduled tests; we also support a 7-day notice for larger scopes. We offer ephemeral staging credentials scoped to the assessment and timeboxed with privilege elevation controls.

Hi Dana — quick follow-up from the assurance side with a concrete delivery plan. We're proposing the following evidence-onramp matrix for Acme Health: 

- Week 0 (kickoff): intake call, confirm scope (environments, CI/CD pipelines to include), and identify data sensitivity bands.
- Week 1–2: evidence deliveries: SOC 2 Type II report (if in retention), architecture diagram, network segmentation summary, list of third-party sub-processors, and sanitized sample logs (rolling 7-day).
- Ongoing cadence: monthly operational summaries (change logs, token-level anomaly reports), quarterly penetration-test summary (findings and mitigations), and annual full SOC 2 attestations.

If your procurement wants a different tempo (e.g., weekly evidence bundles for a limited onboarding period) we can accommodate for a defined onboarding window. On staging access: we will require a Statement of Work addendum that defines the test scope and rollback criteria; Laura, I'll sync with you to draft that language.

Action items:
- Dana: confirm desired initial evidence tempo (standard vs accelerated onboarding).
- Laura: will prepare MSA/order form redline callouts and a short SOW template for ephemeral staging.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Security & Assurance
Redwood Inference
